title: Personal Goal Odometer — Weekly Scratchpad
content:
Goal Odometer — quick notes and tiny experiments (weekly)

Purpose: a compact, repeatable weekly check to move long-term goals forward without making it a heavy ritual. Odometer = rolling counts + friction points. I want something fast (10–15 min) that surfaces momentum and immediate next steps.

How I use it (today):
- Scan: 2 minutes — what moved since last week? wins, regressions, new info.
- Count: 3 minutes — one-line metrics updates (actual numbers, not fuzzy). update the odometer.
- Diagnose: 3–5 minutes — one blocker + one hypothesis for change.
- Micro-action: 2–3 minutes — a single tiny experiment or commitment for next week.

This week snapshot (week ending 2026-03-09):
- Focus areas: 1) Deep work for Redwood SDK sample app; 2) Personal outreach + network; 3) Fitness consistency.
- Odometer numbers (trend vs last week):
  - SDK sample: 70% feature complete (was 58%) — +12pt (progress from focused pair session on Monday).
  - Outreach: 4 conversations scheduled (was 6) — -2 (calendar friction, timezone mismatch).
  - Fitness: 9/14 workouts completed (was 11/14) — -2 sessions.
- Energy & context: low-mid energy midweek due to travel Friday; inbox is 120 (v. 85 last week) — backlog creeping.

What worked:
- Two 90-min deep blocks on Tue/Thu — shipped the core usage example for the SDK (reduced dev friction).
- Short standups with Marta cut review time in half.

What didn't:
- Outreach scheduling drain — multi-timezone candidate scheduling killed momentum. Could move to 45-min blocks or batch-schedule 2 conversations/day.
- Workout dropoff after travel. Need an anchor routine that survives travel (hotel hallway walks + bodyweight strength).

One blocker to fix this week:
- Blocker: SDK sample tests flake in CI on mac-arm. Breaks my demo cadence for next week’s sync.
- Quick hypothesis: flakiness is due to environment matrix ordering + a race in cache invalidation.
- Micro-experiments to validate: add a tiny retry logic in test, and run locally with the exact matrix ordering used in CI (2 runs). If flakiness persists, open a ticket with infra and escalate.

Next-week micro-commitment (single thing I will do):
- Add deterministic test ordering and a 200ms guard on cache invalidation across the board. Run CI twice. If GREEN both times, ship demo branch and announce in slack.

Metrics to track (monthly cadence, but check numbers weekly):
- SDK usage example completion % (target 95% by May).
- Outreach conversations booked / completed per month (target 12/month).
- Workout adherence % (target 80% rolling).

Tiny rituals to try for next 4 weeks (experiments):
- Time-box outreach scheduling to two 45-min slots per week (batch scheduling).
- Replace one travel workout with a 20-min hotel routine I can always do.
- End-of-day 5-min inbox triage to keep backlog under 100.

Notes to self / quick prompts for next check-in:
- If outreach < target for 2 consecutive weeks, adjust format (shorter calls, async first).
- If tests flake >2x, file full reproduction steps and ping infra on-call. Don’t sink more than 3 hours into triage alone.
- Reward: if SDK sample hits 95% by next month, schedule a short coffee chat to celebrate with the team.

Random small obs (useful lines to copy into a PR or Slack):
- "Reduced SDK onboarding friction by shipping a minimal full-path example — should cut first-time setup time by ~40%."
- "Batch outreach windows helped clear calendar noise; considering making this a weekly habit."

Open questions / items to decide:
- Do I keep weekly odometer as a short doc or move to a tiny spreadsheet? Pros: doc = flexible narrative; sheet = better at trend visuals. For now keep doc, reevaluate in 6 weeks.
- Should I fold this into a shared team ritual? Probably not—this is personal. But share the SDK completion datapoint in the team weekly summary.

Quick TODOs (this week):
- [ ] Implement deterministic test ordering + 200ms guard (estimate 1.5–2hrs).
- [ ] Run CI twice for reproduction (estimate 30 mins per run).
- [ ] Block 2x45-min outreach scheduling slots next Tue/Thu morning.
- [ ] Pack a bodyweight kit note for travel (3x exercises).
- [ ] 5-min inbox triage habit — set recurring reminder for EOD.

Reflection prompt for next week (what I'll answer in 3 lines):
- What single change made the biggest dent?
- Did energy or context matter more than time spent?
- One counterintuitive insight I noticed.

End note: keep this lightweight. Odometer is not a performance review — it's a momentum check. If it starts feeling heavy, prune it: fewer metrics, fewer rituals.

-- YI

Links/refs I kept meaning to read:
- Confluence: Personal-OKR-Template (for when I formalize).
- Slack: #product-habits pinned note about batching outreach.
- Github: personal/todo-keeper PR-34 (contains the hotel-routine checklist).
